title: AI-Agents for Culturally Diverse Online Higher Education Environments

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review and conceptual evaluation of how AI tutoring systems can mitigate cultural biases embedded in training data by using context-aware, multi-modal frameworks, cultural memory, and culturally appropriate non-verbal communication.

Conceptual analysis of the accessibility and pedagogical trade-offs of AI agents, specifically evaluating the prohibitive costs of embodied robot tutors for students from under-resourced backgrounds compared to free virtual tutors.
Review of existing literature on inclusive design principles and the use of adaptive AI to personalize learning and provide equal access for students with disabilities and psychological challenges.
